newsitem.title: USA: Rupiah drops in U.S. trading after Suharto rumors. [CORRECTED 22:27 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Rupiah drops in U.S. trading after Suharto rumors. [CORRECTED 22:27 GMT]

text.p: Rumors, later denied, that Indonesia's aging leader Suharto had a heart attack knocked the rupiah in nervous U.S. trading, currency traders said.
The ruphia fell from 2,398 per U.S. dollar to 2,412, before trimming losses. At 1225 EST/1725 GMT, it was quoted 2,402/2,407. (Corrects rupiah figures).
Official sources in Jakarta denied the rumors, saying the president merely suffered from a cold.
"The market hasn't returned to its earlier level, showing that people are still fearful," said a dealer at a money center bank.
Suharto has been in poor health and the rumor touched a sensitive nerve, the dealer said.
Often compared to former China's leader Deng Xiaoping, Suharto has dominated Indonesian politics and economics for decades, dealers said.
"Foreign investors are nervous," said a dealer. "You could see more disinvestment from Indonesia."
Another dealer said the rumor hit the London market near the close when the volume was light, and the selling continued in U.S. trading.
The Thai baht, and to a less extent the Malaysian ringgit, also came under light pressure, he said.
